tasks.scoring: Score 0 if at any moment the yellow, green or orange box's plug is more than 5 cm (3D) from where it lay at the start, whether picked up, pushed or slid by a tug on its cable (tape marks; judged from the top-camera video), or the red box's plug lies in the blue holder or the blue box's plug in the red holder; also 0 if a cable is pulled out of its box (its end at the box moves more than 1 cm). Boxes, cover, posts and holders are fixed to the table. A plug lies in a holder when it is between the holder's side walls, lying on the table, inside the slot or sticking out of its open far end by at most 1 cm. Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 if the red box's plug lies in the red holder and the blue box's plug in the blue holder, each released (no gripper within 3 cm of its centre); 0.5 if exactly one of the two lies released in its own holder; 0 otherwise, including doing nothing. Success (1.0) once the full condition has held for 1 s with both plugs at rest.

tasks.title: Square a milling vise by sweeping its fixed jaw with an indicator
tasks.instruction: Square the vise fixed jaw to the traverse axis and secure the base. Confirm its alignment with the indicator. Leave both grippers clear. All machinery is unpowered.
tasks.context: A fixed jaw at four degrees introduces about 4.2 mm of lateral error across 60 mm of travel. Work located against it inherits that angle. Checking and aligning workholding fixtures is a documented setup duty for machinists and CNC operators and multiple machine tool setters.
tasks.scoring: Score 0 before a complete contact sweep. The carriage must enter the regions at or below -30 mm and at or above +30 mm and pass within 2 mm of centre. During measurement plunger displacement must remain between -6 and +0.5 mm and travel within 40 mm of centre. A valid sweep earns 0.25 or 0.5 if the reading span is at most 0.50 mm. A span at most 0.20 mm earns 0.75 if the adjustment hand is clear throughout the sweep and the clamp pad stays in contact with 0.25 to 5.5 mm spring compression. During verification jaw yaw may vary by at most 0.1 degree and swivel centre displacement by at most 0.10 mm. Score 1 after both hands stay open and clear and the secured rotor remains below 8 mm/s equivalent rim speed for one second. Releasing the clamp or losing alignment invalidates verification. Permanent zero for any nonfinite sample or centre displacement above 0.50 mm.

tasks.title: Trim three overgrown shoots off a box hedge with hedge shears, without cutting the flowers
tasks.instruction: Trim the three tall green shoots off the box hedge with the hedge shears, cutting each just above the hedge, without cutting the flowers. Then leave the shears lying closed on the mat and take both arms back to where they started.
tasks.context: Gardeners trim hedges with two-handed hedge shears: each blade is worked by its own handle, so the blades open and close only when both handles are moved against each other, and the cut has to miss the plants that should stay.
tasks.scoring: Judged from the whole trial. A shoot is trimmed when the shears sever it within 1.8 cm of its cut height (2 cm above the hedge); a flower is cut when the shears sever it anywhere along its stem above the hedge. In a real trial severing is observed directly: the stem's top comes away. In the simulation, where blades do not sever stems by contact, a stem counts as severed when the blades, open at least 20 degrees with the stem between them 2.5 to 15 cm from the pivot, close to 6 degrees open or less while it is still there; its top is then freed and falls. A severed stem stays severed. The shears lie closed on the mat when their pivot is over the mat (at least 2 cm in from its edges), no more than 1.2 cm higher than when they lie flat, the blades within 10 degrees of level and open 6 degrees or less. 0.0 once either flower has been cut. Otherwise 1.0: all three shoots cut, the shears lying closed on the mat and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start), at the end; 0.5: all three shoots cut; 0.25: at least one shoot cut; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the shears still.

tasks.title: Bend a copper tube to 90 degrees in a lever bender, allowing for springback
tasks.instruction: Bend the tube in the bender to the 90 degree mark on the card, judged with the lever fully relaxed, then take both grippers away.
tasks.context: Refrigeration mechanics (O*NET 49-9021.00) and plumbers (47-2152.00) bend copper tube to an angle by hand. It is hard because tubes that look alike spring back by different amounts, seen only when the lever is relaxed, and a bend cannot be undone: pull, relax, read, and pull again.
tasks.scoring: Measured with the protractor card, a ruler and a video. 1.0 when the tube lies in the red band, from 87 to 93 degrees; the lever tip is within 1.5 cm of its start line, in line with the form handle; and both grippers are 3 cm clear of both handles, all still for 1 s. 0.5 when the lever tip is within 1.5 cm of its start line and both grippers are 3 cm clear, all still for 1 s, and the tube reads from 80 to under 87, or over 93 up to 96. 0.25 when the lever tip is within 1.5 cm of its start line and both grippers are 3 cm clear, all still for 1 s, and the tube reads from 70 to under 80. 0 otherwise, or if the tube reads past 96 degrees, or the bender leaves the bench or tips over.

tasks.title: Turn each carton's label toward a fixed scanner as the cartons ride a moving line
tasks.instruction: Before each carton reaches the scanner gate, turn it on its carrier so that its shipping label faces the scanner on the far side of the line. Leave each carton standing upright on its own carrier, and let go of it before it reaches the gate.
tasks.context: On parcel and warehouse lines a fixed scanner reads the barcode on one side of each passing carton; a carton whose label faces elsewhere is a no-read and goes to manual handling, so workers beside the line turn cartons label-out as they go by, without stopping the line or knocking them off. Done by: parcel sorters, warehouse line operators, induction workers.
tasks.scoring: Each carton is read once, at the moment its carrier's centre reaches the gate (y = 0.50). It is read if at that moment: it stands on its own carrier (its centre within 3 cm of the carrier's centre in each of x and y, its underside within 1 cm of the carrier's top); it is upright (its top within 10 degrees of straight up; lying on a side or upside down fails); both grippers' grasp points (between the fingers) are 8 cm or more from its centre; its label faces within 20 degrees of straight at the scanner (+x, seen from above); and it has never touched the table (its lowest corner within 1 cm of the table top) during the trial. Score: one third per carton read (0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1). The trial ends with 1.0 once all three have been read (held 1 s). No carton starts readable (each label is 90 or 180 degrees off), so doing nothing scores 0.

tasks.title: Move a pot off a lit burner and switch the burner off
tasks.instruction: move the coffee pot off the hot burner onto the plate, and leave the stove safe
tasks.context: Cooking fires often start at a burner left on after the pot comes off. Moving the pot is the stated job; switching the burner off is the part 'leave the stove safe' asks for without spelling out.
tasks.scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. The switch is off when the knob's centre is within 1.5 cm of the OFF end of its travel (12 cm left). The pot is on the plate when it stands still with its centre within 5 cm of the plate's centre and its base no more than 2 cm above the plate. 1.0: the pot is on the plate and the switch is off. 0.5: the switch is off and the pot stands still on the table at least 12 cm from the burner's centre, but not on the plate. 0.25: the pot is on the plate but the switch is not off (burner left on), or the switch is off but the pot still stands on the burner. 0.0: anything else, including the pot fallen, tipped or off the table, or nothing done.

tasks.title: Free the ice cubes: twist an ice-cube tray between both hands, then turn it over to tip the cubes into the dish
tasks.instruction: Get the ice cubes into the glass dish: hold the ice-cube tray by its two end tabs and twist it, one end one way and the other end the other way, so the frozen cubes crack loose; then lift it off the dish's rim, turn it over above the dish so all eight cubes fall in, turn it back and set it back across the dish, and take both arms back to where they started.
tasks.context: Getting ice out of a tray is a small everyday kitchen job at home, in bars and in care homes: the cubes are frozen to the plastic and only come loose when the tray is twisted, one end against the other, which takes both hands; then the tray has to be turned over above a bowl without dropping cubes on the counter.
tasks.scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 1.0: all eight cubes in the dish, the tray back across the dish (each end tab within 1.5 cm of where it started, at its height within 1 cm, upright within 15 degrees) and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre, TCP, within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: all eight cubes in the dish, otherwise; 0.25: the tray twisted far enough to crack the cubes loose at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the tray and every cube still.

tasks.title: Fit a U-joint cross longer than its yoke's ear gap: push one journal through, swing it level, slide it back to centre
tasks.instruction: Install the orange cross in the blue yoke: push one of its two flat journals through one ear's hole, swing the cross level so the other flat journal lines up with the other ear's hole, then slide it back until both journals are in their holes by the same depth.
tasks.context: Spicer Driveshafts Service Manual DSSM3264 (September 2007), Reassembly - Snap Ring Design, page 17, steps 2 and 3: "Position the journal cross in the yoke cross holes" and "Move one end of the journal cross to cause a trunnion to project through the cross hole beyond the outer machined face of the yoke ear." https://www.truckid.com/images/spicer/pdf/driveshafts-service-manual.pdf Done by: driveline and heavy-truck service technicians. The task ends at step 2, the cross sitting in both holes; until it does, no bearing cup can go on.
tasks.scoring: Either pair of journals can be the one that goes in; the pair nearer the holes' axis is scored. A journal is in its hole when the cross's centre is between the ears' inner faces, the journal's tip is at least 1 mm past its ear's inner face, and the tip's centre is within 8 mm of the holes' axis (inside a hole it can be 6 mm off at most). Installed: both journals of the pair in their holes, each tip at least 3.5 mm past its ear's inner face (6.6 mm when centred, so within 3.1 mm of centred), and the pair within 5 degrees of the holes' axis. 1.0 when installed and still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s, which ends the trial. Otherwise the last step scores 0.75 if installed, 0.5 if both journals are in their holes (off centre or turned), 0.25 if one is, else 0. A cross pushed deep into one ear with its other journal out scores 0.25; one on the ears' tops, outside the yoke or in the holder scores 0. The scorer does not see the grippers, so a cross held in place counts the same as one let go.

tasks.title: Fit up two bevelled coupons for a V-groove weld, bevels facing and a 1/16-1/8 in root opening
tasks.instruction: Fit up the two steel coupons for a single-V groove butt weld: turn each one so its bevelled edge (the bright one) faces the other coupon, and set them flat side by side with a root opening of 1/16 to 1/8 inch (1.6 to 3.2 mm) along the whole joint and their ends in line.
tasks.context: Welders and fitters set two prepared plates with their bevels facing each other and a set root opening before the root pass: "Root Opening: 1/16\"-1/8\"" (LANL WPS 3501-11B, an AWS groove-weld procedure: https://engstandards.lanl.gov/esm/welding/welding_specs/3501-11B.pdf), and "Parts to be joined by butt welding shall be carefully aligned" (LANL WFP 2-04, AWS D1.1, 8.0 D). Too tight leaves the root unfused, too wide burns through, and a coupon turned the wrong way puts a square edge in the joint. Done by: welders, cutters, solderers and brazers; structural metal fabricators and fitters.
tasks.scoring: A coupon is flat when tilted at most 5 degrees with its centre within 3 mm of its height lying on the table, and still when moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s. A coupon's bevel faces the other when the other's centre lies ahead of its bevelled edge and within that edge's length. The root opening is measured at both ends of the joint, from each coupon's root edge (the bottom of its bevelled side) to the other coupon's bevelled side. 1.0 when both coupons are flat and still, both bevels face each other, the root opening is 1.6 to 3.2 mm at both ends and the ends are in line within 5 mm, held for 1 s; if time runs out before that has held for 1 s, it scores 0.9. 0.5 when both are flat and still with both bevels facing each other, parallel within 10 degrees, opening 0 to 10 mm at both ends and ends within 2 cm, but the opening or the ends are outside those limits. 0.25 when both are flat and still, side by side as for 0.5, with only one bevel facing the joint (a square edge in the joint). Otherwise 0, including a coupon off the table, on edge or on top of the other. The joint can be anywhere on the table, run any way, with either coupon on either side.

tasks.title: Wrap a pipe thread with thread-seal tape from a dispenser, the way the fitting turns on
tasks.instruction: Wrap the pipe's thread with thread-seal tape, ready for the fitting to be screwed on, then put the dispenser back on its mat.
tasks.context: Every taper-threaded pipe joint is sealed this way before a fitting goes on: the tape is wound the way the fitting will turn on (clockwise seen from the thread's end), three to six turns over the thread, leaving the first thread bare so no shreds get into the pipe, and its torn end pressed down. Wound the other way, the tape bunches and unwinds as the fitting is screwed on and the joint leaks. Done by: plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (O*NET 47-2152.00), maintenance workers (49-9071.00).
tasks.scoring: Measured on the thread at the end: count the turns, look at the direction, and a ruler on the thread. 0 if the tape is wound anticlockwise (seen from the thread's end) or less than one turn is on the thread. 1.0 if it is wound clockwise 3 to 6 turns; covers every part of the thread from 1 mm above its shoulder to 4 mm below the pipe's end; no tape is within 1 mm of the end; it is torn off the roll with its tail pressed down on the wrap; the dispenser is back upright on its mat, with no part of either gripper within 1 cm of it, still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. 0.5 if the tape is wound and torn off as for 1.0 but the tail is left standing or the dispenser is not back on its mat or not released; 0.25 if it is wound clockwise at least one turn on the thread; else 0.

tasks.title: Flex a 3D printer's build plate with both hands to pop a printed robot part free, without kinking it
tasks.instruction: Get the printed part off the build plate and into the bin: flex the plate by its side edges until the part pops free, and leave the plate flat on its stand.
tasks.context: Every robot part printed in-house comes off a spring-steel build plate by hand: the plate is bent away under the part, both sides at once, until it lets go. Bending it the other way squeezes the part, and bending it too sharply kinks the steel so it no longer lies flat for the next print. A robot that can do this can clear the printers making its own parts.
tasks.scoring: 0 if, at any time, the plate bends more sharply than a 15 cm radius anywhere (more than 20 degrees across any 52 mm of its width: kinked), any of five points on its left-to-right centre line (its middle and 52 and 103 mm each side) drops 2 cm below the stand's top, or the part comes down on the bench outside the bin (its centre under 3 cm above the bench); 0 unless the plate and the part moved under 1 mm in the last second. Otherwise 0.25 once the part has been freed (the plate under both of its ends turned 6 degrees or more from the plate's middle at once, edges down); 0.5 with the part in the bin; 0.75 with the plate also back flat on its stand (every point within 10 mm of where it started and 3 mm of its height, flat within 3 degrees); 1.0 with every fingertip also 8 cm or more from the plate and the part.
